This database tells the state's story: from its first peoples through statehood to the modern era, plus the famous sons and daughters, the industries, and the facts every resident should know.

title: Statehood
description: Montana achieved statehood 1889 (41st). The road to statehood ran through territorial government, population thresholds, and a congressional enabling act — the standard American path. Copper kings; homesteading. Statehood Day is still celebrated, and the admission order gives Montana its number among the states.

title: The statehood story

description: The statehood story of Montana: settlement, territorial organization, the push for admission, and finally the star on the flag. Big Sky country. Every state's admission reflected the national politics of its era — Montana's story is no exception, and it explains much about the state's character today.

title: Capital: Helena
d: Helena is the capital of Montana.
definition: Helena is the capital of Montana.
description: Helena has been the seat of Montana government, home to the capitol building, the supreme court, and the legislature. Capitals are often not the biggest city — Montana's largest is Billings — chosen instead for geography or politics. Visit the capitol: the building itself tells the state's story in stone.

title: Nickname: Treasure State
description: The nickname "Treasure State" captures how Montana sees itself — and how America sees it. Copper kings and homesteaders shaped the Treasure State. State nicknames come from history, geography, or industry, and they appear on license plates, tourism campaigns, and sports teams. The motto goes deeper: "Oro y plata (Gold and silver)."

title: Motto: Oro y plata (Gold and silver)
t: Motto: Oro y plata (Gold and silver)
d: The state motto of Montana is "Oro y plata (Gold and silver)."
definition: The state motto of Montana is "Oro y plata (Gold and silver)."
description: The motto "Oro y plata (Gold and silver)" is Montana's official creed, adopted by the legislature and carried on the state seal. Seal with mountains and mining tools on blue. Mottos distill a state's ideals into a phrase — learn it, and you understand what the state aspires to be.
